exercises.title: An adjacency list
exercises.task: Read Graph: a map from each node to the list of nodes it points to. Run builds the import graph of a few Go packages (main -> fmt means main imports fmt), prints what each package imports, then the reverse graph: who imports it.

exercises.title: Build the graph
exercises.task: Fill Build: read lines A -> B and add the edge. Every node that appears, even only on the right, must be a key of the graph, with an empty list if it points nowhere.
hints: Make sure B exists as a key too: if _, ok := g[b]; !ok { g[b] = nil }.
Then g[a] = append(g[a], b): appending to a missing key works, it starts from nil.

exercises.title: Leaves and roots
exercises.task: In the import graph of a program, list the leaves (packages that import nothing: the compiler can build them first, with nothing else ready) and the roots (packages that nothing imports: the programs themselves, or dead code). Both lists sorted.
hints: Leaf: the node's own list is empty.
Root: it never appears in anyone's list. Count the incoming edges (the in-degree) in a map.
sort.Strings before returning: map iteration order is random.
